key_insight: The paper shows that, on edge hardware, the main energy bottleneck in VLM inference is often the language/decoder side rather than the vision encoder. In other words: seeing is comparatively cheap, while speaking is what costs the most energy.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a clear, systematic understanding of where energy is actually spent during on-device Vision-Language Model inference, challenging the common assumption that reducing visual tokens is the primary path to efficiency.
method: Performs the first systematic energy profiling of edge VLM inference across multiple model families, input resolutions, and hardware platforms.
Compares energy costs between visual processing and language generation to identify the true dominant bottleneck.
Analyzes how architecture choice and input resolution affect energy use, enabling more accurate optimization targets.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes edge-optimization strategy: focusing only on fewer visual tokens may miss the biggest energy savings. The findings can guide better model design, deployment decisions, and hardware-aware optimization for embodied and mobile AI systems.

paper_title: Seeing is Free, Speaking is Not: Uncovering the True Energy Bottleneck in Edge VLM Inference
paper_authors: Junfei Zhan, Haoxun Shen, Mingang Guo, Zixuan Huang, Tengjiao He
